findings.description: `pr/review-open` only reads the `claude-review` status on the current head, but the poster's `N important finding(s)` counts only that round's new importants. So the next push drops the label whether or not the importants were fixed. An incremental review never re-raises earlier importants, and a comment-only push gets no review at all. Either way the PR goes back to `pr/ready` with the importants still unresolved.
findings.body:
**The label disappears on the next push even if the importants are still open.**

The new check reads only the head's status description:

```js
const review = combined.statuses.find((s) => s.context === "claude-review");
if (review?.state === "success" && /\d+ important finding/.test(review.description ?? "")) {
  return "pr/review-open";
}
```

The count in that description covers only the findings the latest round raised. In `tools/review/src/post-review.script.ts`, `importants = anchored.length + unanchored.length` (line 228) is built from `summary.findings` filtered to `tag === "important"`, and the poster never reads `prior_importants`. Two common paths leave earlier importants open and still take the label off:

1. **Incremental review after a code push.** `.claude/skills/pr-ci-review/SKILL.md` §3 marks each prior important `resolved` or `unresolved` in `prior_importants` and says to "never re-post or re-raise one". An unresolved prior important is therefore not in `findings`. The new head gets `success` / `no blocking issues`, and pr-status returns `pr/ready`. This happens on a push that fixes only one of two importants, and on an unrelated push.
2. **Comment-only push.** `tools/review/src/review-preflight.script.ts:204` puts a `pending` status of `Not reviewed: only comments and prose changed since …` on the new head and skips the review. pr-status already skips a pending status starting with "Not reviewed" (lines 139-143), so the PR falls through to `pr/ready`.

In practice `pr/review-open` means "the latest round found new importants", not "the review has open importants". The pushes that should be checked against it are exactly the ones that clear it. `src/core/ci-wait.service.ts:235-264` covers both cases on purpose, using the open review threads and an `isOnHead` check.

Possible fix: count the unresolved review threads the poster opened on the PR, using GraphQL `reviewThreads { isResolved ... }` (pr-status already has `pull-requests: write`). Keep the description check as a fallback for a round whose findings were all unanchored.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/986191ad745a8c39bfd57a0e72ad7a9b1c1ce1f3/.github/workflows/pr-status.yml#L118-L124

findings.description: Optional: the WHY comment spends half its length on how `pup fix` uses the status, which this workflow doesn't touch. "The poster sets `success` on every run it posted, findings or not, so the findings are read from the description" carries the same reason.

A `success` status of `partial review: no blocking issues` still ends at `pr/ready`, but the poster says a quick or area-restricted pass is no merge signal (`post-review.script.ts:230-231`), and `ci-wait.service.ts:262` only treats the exact clean-review description as ready to merge.

process_issues.description: The validator's `gh pr view --json` call was refused by the CI command lock. It got the PR body from a bare `gh pr view 259` instead, so its verdict was not affected.
